sources.measurement_family: Online Nation digital audience and time
sources.coverage: Online adult internet activity and YouTube use; press summary does not give every underlying weighting and device denominator

sources.measurement_family: Barb in-home video viewing and weekly audience measures as presented by Ofcom
sources.coverage: In-home Wi-Fi devices and TV sets; explicitly excludes out-of-home and cellular viewing for in-home video series

sources.measurement_family: Digital News Report online news audience survey
sources.coverage: Online respondents and market averages, not a population-weighted worldwide census

observations.population: UK adults in Ofcom Online Nation study
observations.device_scope: online platforms; TV viewing not included in time statistics
observations.frequency: use within Ofcom survey measurement; not a lifetime or daily rate without method
observations.definition_notes: The press summary states YouTube was used by 94% of UK adults; it is not the percentage of all global users from the UK.
observations.limits: Full weighting, coverage and exact reach window require report table consultation; do not treat as worldwide monthly active users.

observations.population: Audience captured by Ofcom Online Nation online-time measurement
observations.metric: Reported average YouTube time excluding the television set
observations.definition_notes: The press release does not fully specify conditional user versus all-adult denominator; retain this uncertainty.
observations.limits: Cannot add to or subtract from Ofcom's separate Barb in-home all-device estimates.

observations.population: Persons in Barb in-home viewing measure
observations.metric: Average YouTube time on a television set
observations.definition_notes: One point in Ofcom's Barb-based 2022 versus 2025 TV-set series.
observations.limits: Does not measure mobile, desktop, out-of-home or mobile-network viewing.

observations.population: Persons in Barb in-home viewing measure
observations.metric: Average YouTube time on a television set
observations.definition_notes: Comparable to 2022 TV-set measure in the same published series.
observations.limits: Does not measure mobile, desktop, out-of-home or mobile-network viewing.

observations.population: Persons in Barb in-home viewing measure
observations.metric: YouTube time on all connected devices at home
observations.definition_notes: Same Ofcom/Barb in-home family as 2025 observation.
observations.limits: Excludes outside-home and viewing over cellular networks; includes TV viewing, so do not add TV-set minutes again.

observations.population: Persons in Barb in-home viewing measure
observations.metric: YouTube time on all connected devices at home
observations.definition_notes: Includes TV viewing; not comparable without caveats to Online Nation internet-only time.
observations.limits: Excludes outside-home and viewing over cellular networks.

observations.population: People aged 75 and older in Ofcom-reported weekly video-reach estimate
observations.device_scope: weekly video reach measured in Media Nations 2026 family
observations.definition_notes: Not a percentage of all YouTube users and not a daily use estimate.
observations.limits: Age-group population estimates must not be summed with general adult reach.

observations.population: People aged 75 and older in Ofcom-reported weekly video-reach estimate
observations.device_scope: weekly video reach measured in Media Nations 2026 family
observations.definition_notes: Age-cohort prevalence, not audience age composition.
observations.limits: Do not infer individual older viewers' identities or their content preferences.

observations.population: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026 online survey respondents in 48 markets
observations.frequency: survey reported use; exact lookback must follow survey instrument
observations.definition_notes: Report labels 69% YouTube use for any purpose. It is not a population-weighted worldwide penetration or UK adult rate.
observations.limits: Online samples underrepresent those without internet in many countries; market averages do not constitute a world census.

observations.population: Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026 online survey respondents in 48 markets
observations.metric: YouTube use for news in the previous week
observations.definition_notes: News use is a subset of use for any purpose under Reuters survey definitions, not the share of YouTube traffic classified as news.
observations.limits: Cannot be called the share of global people watching YouTube news; weighted market averages/online respondents differ from Pew U.S. adults.

valid_series.comparison: same family, geography, device and unit; time change only
same in-home video family; includes television
age-group prevalence on a weekly basis only

excluded_comparisons: Never add 51 Online Nation minutes to 41 Barb in-home minutes as if disjoint viewing periods.
Never add 19 TV-set minutes to 41 in-home all-device minutes; the latter includes television.
Never compare 94% UK adult use to 69% across 48 online survey markets as if equally sampled populations.
Never identify UK age 75+ weekly reach as the age composition of a YouTube user census.
Never present 34% multi-market news use as a fraction of YouTube video impressions or watch hours.
Do not combine market reach percentages to estimate an overall unique worldwide audience size.
